purpose: Prevent Skyrim camera and gameplay controls from consuming mouse/keyboard events while the RazKolbas diagnostics menu is visible.

original.validation: The opcode, eight-byte argument setup and nineteen-byte continuation must match exactly. The rel32 displacement is decoded at runtime because an existing compatible hook may own the call. Both the immediate target and a recognized FF 25 absolute relay destination must be committed executable memory.

replacement.representation: E8 rel32 to a W^X near relay; relay is FF 25 00000000 followed by the absolute RazKolbas proxy address

abi.arguments: RCX is the existing input dispatcher; RDX is InputEvent* const*
abi.behavior: The proxy calls the previous hook chain exactly once. It forwards the original event list when the menu is hidden and a static one-element null list when the menu is visible and focused.
abi.registers_stack_return: The generated relay changes no registers or flags. The C++ proxy follows the platform ABI and returns the prior chain's void result.

lifetime.installation: SKSEPlugin_Load startup boundary before world/input threads run
lifetime.ownership: The plugin DLL is pinned and the sealed relay remains allocated for process lifetime.
lifetime.removal: No hot removal; disabling takes effect on the next launch.

recovery.disable: Add skyrim1170.menu-input-dispatch-v1 to Patching.DisabledPatchIds or disable experimental versioned patches, then restart Skyrim.
recovery.failure_scope: Any identity, surrounding-code, executable-chain, relay-allocation or exact-write mismatch leaves the call unchanged and logs the rejection.

evidence: 2026-09-24 user test: 0.1.68 wrote ControlMap::ignoreKeyboardMouse at verified AE +0x129, but camera movement continued.
Live 1.6.1170 disassembly: Address Library ID 68617 resolved to RVA 0xcd8f40 and the dispatch CALL is at +0x7b/RVA 0xcd8fbb.
The active call already chained through an executable SKSE relay to SmartTalk.dll; the new patch preserves that target as its next owner.
DynamicShaderFrameGen reference uses the same dispatch boundary and a null event list while its menu is visible.
Unit tests cover exact caller validation, variable prior-owner displacement, empty-list selection, chained target decoding and invalid plans.
